title: Offset-tracking Kuperberg subtraction sieve with phase estimation

claims.statement: For the offset-tracking Kuperberg subtraction sieve with Kitaev phase estimation (OTS) in proof.md, with its fixed parameters m = ceil(2 sqrt(n)), r = ceil(n/m), M = 72 ceil(log2(48n)), lambda_r = 2^(m+2) + 8M 2^(ceil((r-1)/2)), L0 = 16^r lambda_r, QFT precision delta = 1/(12 n L0), and deterministic cutoff: for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), worst-case total work in the challenge model (including source cost, approximate-QFT generation and Clifford+T synthesis, classical sorting and addressing, and all discarded and failed work) is T(N,s) = O(2^(5 sqrt(n))) with an absolute constant; the uniform envelope B_T(n) = 2^(5 n^(1/2)) has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds of the same algorithm and configuration, on every execution branch, with unconditional full-secret success probability at least 3/4 for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, where n = ceil(log2 N).

For the offset-tracking Kuperberg subtraction sieve with Kitaev phase estimation (OTS) in proof.md, with its fixed parameters m = ceil(2 sqrt(n)), r = ceil(n/m), M = 72 ceil(log2(48n)), lambda_r = 2^(m+2) + 8M 2^(ceil((r-1)/2)), L0 = 16^r lambda_r, QFT precision delta = 1/(12 n L0), and deterministic cutoff: for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), worst-case peak classical workspace is S_C(N,s) = O(2^(4 sqrt(n)) n) bits with an absolute constant; the envelope B_C(n) = 2^(4 n^(1/2)) n has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds of the same algorithm and configuration, on every execution branch, with unconditional full-secret success probability at least 3/4 for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, where n = ceil(log2 N).

For the offset-tracking Kuperberg subtraction sieve with Kitaev phase estimation (OTS) in proof.md, with its fixed parameters m = ceil(2 sqrt(n)), r = ceil(n/m), M = 72 ceil(log2(48n)), lambda_r = 2^(m+2) + 8M 2^(ceil((r-1)/2)), L0 = 16^r lambda_r, QFT precision delta = 1/(12 n L0), and deterministic cutoff: for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), worst-case peak quantum workspace is S_Q(N,s) = O(2^(4 sqrt(n))) qubits with an absolute constant; the envelope B_Q(n) = 2^(4 n^(1/2)) has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds of the same algorithm and configuration, on every execution branch, with unconditional full-secret success probability at least 3/4 for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, where n = ceil(log2 N).

For the offset-tracking Kuperberg subtraction sieve with Kitaev phase estimation (OTS) in proof.md, with its fixed parameters m = ceil(2 sqrt(n)), r = ceil(n/m), M = 72 ceil(log2(48n)), lambda_r = 2^(m+2) + 8M 2^(ceil((r-1)/2)), L0 = 16^r lambda_r, QFT precision delta = 1/(12 n L0), and deterministic cutoff: for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the total number of fresh DCP source copies acquired on every execution branch, counting every discarded copy and every copy used by a failed sieve run, is Q(N,s) <= n L0 = O(2^(4 sqrt(n)) n) with an absolute constant; the envelope B_samples(n) = 2^(4 n^(1/2)) n has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds of the same algorithm and configuration, on every execution branch, with unconditional full-secret success probability at least 3/4 for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, where n = ceil(log2 N).

For the offset-tracking Kuperberg subtraction sieve with Kitaev phase estimation (OTS) in proof.md, with its fixed parameters m = ceil(2 sqrt(n)), r = ceil(n/m), M = 72 ceil(log2(48n)), lambda_r = 2^(m+2) + 8M 2^(ceil((r-1)/2)), L0 = 16^r lambda_r, QFT precision delta = 1/(12 n L0), and deterministic cutoff: the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n) = 0, i.e. all Q acquired source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N >= 2 and every s, full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 3/4 jointly with all four resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted; this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
